comparison: Both strongly support the core finding of protein-water decoupling. OpenEval emphasizes resolution independence of protein Ton (C29-C32) and systematic hydration dependence (C33-C34). Peer reviewers describe data as 'convincing' and 'compelling,' explicitly affirming that 'protein motions are not coupled to the solvent.' Both evaluations converge on supporting the decoupling claim (C3, C56).

Both support the resolution-dependent nature of water transition. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of resolution dependence (C47-C48) and independence from protein structure (C54-C55). Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the 'resolution effect' interpretation, stating the 'apparent water transition temperature is a "resolution effect"; i.e. instrument response is limited.' Complete agreement on this key finding.

Perfect claim overlap (C52-C53). Both support consistency with prior literature showing smooth relaxation behavior. OpenEval notes these are citations rather than new results, serving as corroborating evidence. Peer reviewers accept this consistency and note the work will require 'a reassessment of solvent "slaving",' implicitly accepting the alignment with prior smooth relaxation studies.

Both support the DSC findings and glass transition interpretation. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of DSC evidence (C37-C38, C40-C42) and polymer glass transition analogy (C39, C43, C58). Peer reviewers describe the study as 'well conducted' with 'convincing' data, without raising concerns about DSC measurements or glass transition interpretation, indicating implicit acceptance.

Both address functional implications but with different emphasis. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C62 is supported but C63 is speculative and functional links remain unproven. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the intrinsic nature of the transition and stating 'protein motions are not coupled to the solvent,' but do not critically evaluate the speculative functional claims. Peer review is less critical of mechanistic speculation.

Both strongly support the experimental methodology. OpenEval evaluates isotopic contrast basis (C22-C24) and instrumental setup (C68-C70) as well-established, though notes potential complications not discussed. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the methodology, highlighting 'a lot of effort to acquire the perdeuterated proteins' and the multi-resolution approach as overcoming 'limitations in previous studies.'

Both address MD simulations and hydration effects. OpenEval supports the structural findings (C35-C36) but notes limitations in protein coverage and equilibration time. Peer reviewers do not raise specific concerns about MD simulations, implicitly accepting them as part of the 'well conducted' study. Peer review less critical of simulation limitations than OpenEval.

OpenEval evaluates the explanation for contradictory literature (C60-C61) as SUPPORTED, noting it reconciles conflicting observations through demonstrated resolution dependence. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers' acceptance of the resolution effect interpretation implicitly supports this reconciliation.

OpenEval supports q-range independence (C83) based on Tables 3-5 data, validating that findings are not artifacts of momentum transfer selection. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though this technical validation is encompassed in peer reviewers' overall assessment of 'convincing' data.

OpenEval supports resolution independence findings (C85-C86) through comparison with prior work and the hydrated vs dry protein approach. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though this contributes to the overall resolution independence conclusion that peer reviewers explicitly support.

OpenEval rates MD simulation protocol (C87-C90) as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether 30 ns equilibration is sufficient for low-temperature simulations approaching glass transition. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers do not critically examine simulation equilibration criteria.
